div.p: An XSLT package is a stylesheet module whose root element is xsl:package, with a name - usually a URI - and optionally a package-version. Another stylesheet uses it by name and version, with xsl:use-package, rather than by its file path:
div.code:
<xsl:package name="http://example.com/strings" package-version="2.1" version="3.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"> ... </xsl:package>
<!-- in a stylesheet that uses it --> <xsl:use-package name="http://example.com/strings" package-version="2+"/>
div.p: The package URI is an identifier, not a location: xsl:use-package matches it exactly against the name of each xsl:package, and it isn't resolved like the href of xsl:import. Neither the XSLT specification nor Saxon fixes where a package's file is.

The XSLT/XPath extension finds it, so that the package's declarations are known to the linter, auto-completion, hover help and go to definition - and when a stylesheet is run, passes the packages it uses to Saxon.

figure.figcaption: The XSLT Imports view shows packages used by the current stylesheet, discovered during workspace scanning or declared in workspace settings. Use auto-completion on the name attribute of xsl:use-package to select and import from additional packages available.

div.p: Every .xsl and .xslt file in the workspace whose root element is xsl:package is found automatically, by the same background scan of the workspace that finds the top-level stylesheet importing a module. Its name and version are read from its xsl:package element - a package with no package-version is version 1. These packages need no setting, and they're read again when saved: change a package's name or version, and the stylesheets using it see the change.
div.aside: The workspace scan is turned off with the XSLT.resources.inferParentFromWorkspace setting. Packages are then found only from the XSLT.resources.xsltPackages setting.
div.p: For a package kept outside the workspace, for example a library shared between projects, add its path to the XSLT.resources.xsltPackages setting - relative to the workspace folder, or as a file: URI. The name and version are read from the file, so the path is all that's needed:

An entry can also give a name and version, which are then used instead of those in the file - for example, to try a copy of a package under a different version. Packages from the setting come before those found in the workspace when the same version of a package is in both.

When more than one file declares a package with the same name, the package-version of xsl:use-package chooses between them: the highest version in its range is used. With no package-version, the range is *, so the highest version of all is used.

tr.td: any of the ranges separated by commas

div.p: Versions are compared part by part as numbers, so 1.10 is higher than 1.9, and a missing part counts as 0, so 1 and 1.0.0 are the same version. A version with a name part, such as 3.0-beta, is lower than the same version without one, 3.0.

When a stylesheet that uses packages is run - with Quick Run, an XSLT task for SaxonJ or SaxonC, or the debugger - the package files are passed to Saxon with its -lib option. These are the packages used by the stylesheet, by the modules it imports or includes, and by the packages themselves - each the version chosen as above. Saxon reads each package's name and version from the file, as the extension does, so packages are only ever declared in one place: the packages themselves.
Without this, Saxon reports XTSE3000 Cannot find package for each package used.
div.aside: A task with a configFilename property - a Saxon configuration file - doesn't get the -lib option, as the configuration file may declare the packages itself, in its xsltPackages element. SaxonJS tasks don't get it either.
div.p: An xsl:use-package whose package isn't found - no package with the name, or none with a version in its package-version range - is reported as an error, XTSE3000, as Saxon reports it. Two quick fixes are offered:

ul.li: Create Package '...' - choose where to save a new package file, by default beside the stylesheet and named from the package URI's last part. It has the package's name, and the version the package-version asks for (the lowest, for a range such as 2+)

Add Existing Package File... - pick a package file, for example outside the workspace, to add to the XSLT.resources.xsltPackages setting. Its xsl:package must have the name, and a version in the range

div.p: In the name of an xsl:use-package, auto-completion lists the URIs of the packages found - in the workspace and the XSLT.resources.xsltPackages setting - with each package's versions. In its package-version, it lists * and the versions of the named package, highest first.

The name of an xsl:use-package is a link to the package's file - press ⌘+click to open it. Go to definition, hover help and auto-completion for the package's functions, templates, variables and other declarations work as for an imported module.
